ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g7-arts-and-music-u05-l03

Lesson focus: choreographic structure

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — first supported pass for choreographic structure. 1 INTENT: name what the study should do. 2 SETUP: choose a safe, available route. 3 NOTICE: locate objective, obstacle, gesture, level, distance, pause, pathway, timing, and sequence. 4 ACT: complete one small study using this cue—A pause changes expectation; distance changes relationship; a repeated gesture creates a motif. Each choice gains meaning from what comes before and after it. 5 CHECK: point to the result before using “works” or “does not work.” 6 SECOND STUDY: change one relationship only. Keep both attempts and circle the exact prompt you are ready to remove. Worked example for choreographic structure: START by the table → LOOK toward the exit → PAUSE two counts → WRITE a plan turns four actions into a readable decision. Use it to study choreographic structure; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-created guided scaffold for both supported studies, then mark the prompt you are ready to remove.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant objective, obstacle, gesture, level, distance, pause, pathway, timing, and sequence and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use notation, a cue map, paper blocking, silent gesture, or a private live demonstration to one trusted adult as the target permits. When timing or performance control is the target, prose alone does not claim that evidence; the adult may verify the private attempt without recording it. No microphone, camera, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres a visual element (choreographic structure). Provide tactile, raised-line, or high-relief equivalents, enlarged and high-contrast print, and a verbal description route. Never make colour discrimination alone carry a criterion — pair any colour judgement with value, label, or texture.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.fallback: Use the complete supplied beat map, script, evidence record, or event description. No teacher handout or outside search is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce choreographic structure to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one objective relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact objective evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from objective, obstacle, gesture, level, distance, pause, pathway, timing, and sequence; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply choreographic structure under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on choreographic structure rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What choreographic structure means here
concept_instruction.body: Performance choices make an intention observable through action, timing, space, sound, or stillness.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A pause changes expectation; distance changes relationship; a repeated gesture creates a motif. Each choice gains meaning from what comes before and after it.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A large gesture reads clearly but can reduce subtlety. A restrained choice can invite attention but may need stronger timing or position to remain legible. Worked example: START by the table → LOOK toward the exit → PAUSE two counts → WRITE a plan turns four actions into a readable decision. Non-example: Explaining a character’s feeling without making any choice visible in action, timing, or space does not demonstrate performance evidence.
